pass_a_gloss: If we must next, as you ordered, set forth first the plausible arguments of those who think nothing is accomplished by prayers and call praying superfluous, we will do even this as we can, since prayer's name is now used more commonly and simply by us. [gap.] This doctrine is inglorious, patronless: hardly anyone accepting providence and God-over-all rejects prayer; it belongs to atheists or name-only theists. But the opposing activity, dressing godlessness in Christ's name, has persuaded some not to pray — led by anti-sensible, anti-sacramental Scripture-slanderers. The (providentialist) objectors' arguments: God knows all before birth, nothing newly known [gap: mockery?]; why pray to one who knows needs beforehand (Matt 6:8)? A good father-creator arranges savingly without prayer, like a father of infants; men fall shorter of God than babes of parents' minds. Foreknowledge + predetermination make prayer folly (sunrise) and madness (solstice-to-spring; escaping necessity = melancholy). Womb-estrangement (Ps 57:4), womb-setting-apart (Gal 1:15), pre-birth election (Rom 9:11-13; Jacob/Esau; Moses' refuge Ps 89) make forgiveness/Spirit-seeking vain. Universalized: the elect need no prayer; the non-elect pray myriad times unheard (Eph 1:4-5; Rom 8:29-30 chain with extra 'of glory'; Josiah named beforehand, 1 Kgs 13:2; Judas' prayer sin, Ps 108:7-8, Acts 1:20) [gap ~100 letters]; praying to turn God's purpose or as if he waited to ordain makes him learn from scrutiny [obscure]. Ambrose's letter-formulated dilemmas set as agenda: (1) foreknowledge→vain; (2) divine will unmoved→vain; assumed beforehand for the dissolution of prayer-deterrents.
